evidence_span.text: HAOX2 is expressed predominantly in liver and kidney and displays highest activity toward 2-hydroxypalmitate.

reviews.rationale: Human HAOX2 (the Hao2 ortholog) is biochemically characterized as a liver-expressed peroxisomal 2-hydroxy fatty acid oxidase, gene-specifically supporting the assigned alpha-oxidation function. The finding is in human tissue, a different species from mouse aging/MASLD liver, so the declared partial context is overclaimed (actually indirect).

evidence_span.text: Immunotitration studies using antibodies specific to the alpha class GSTs, GSTA1-1, GSTA2-2, and GSTA3-3, indicate that these GST isozymes account for approximately half of the glutathione peroxidase activity toward phospholipid hydroperoxides present in the 28,000g supernatant fractions of rat and mouse liver extracts.

reviews.rationale: Isozyme-specific immunotitration naming GSTA3-3 in mouse and rat liver directly demonstrates alpha-class GST glutathione-peroxidase antioxidant activity, providing gene-specific support for the assigned function. The mouse-liver hepatocyte system is the target context, so the direct label is accurate.

evidence_span.text: bile acids strongly inhibited the cysteine dioxygenase type-1-mediated (CDO1-mediated) cysteine catabolic pathway

reviews.rationale: CDO1-overexpressing mouse hepatocytes and FXR-dependent modulation establish CDO1 as the mediator of hepatic cysteine catabolism, directly supporting the core assigned function; the unstated taurine-conjugation clause is a broader claim not required of one citation. Mouse liver hepatocytes are the target context, so direct is accurate.

evidence_span.text: WT but not Nrf2−/− liver slices treated with arsenic resulted in increased mRNA levels of the key fructose metabolism pathway enzymes ketohexokinase (Khk), sorbitol dehydrogenase (Sord), and triokinase/FMN cyclase (Tkfc)

reviews.rationale: ChIP-PCR ARE binding and Nrf2-knockout data gene-specifically confirm Sord as an NRF2-regulated hepatic fructose-metabolism gene, supporting the 'under NRF2 regulation' clause, but the study found minimal polyol-pathway flux and did not demonstrate the sorbitol-to-fructose conversion, so support is partial. The arsenic-induced diabetes model is not aging or MASLD, so the declared direct context is overclaimed.
